newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli dollar-linked bonds close higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli dollar-linked bonds close higher.

text.p: Prices of Israeli dollar-linked bonds closed higher on Wednesday, but at a more moderate rate than in previous sessions, as the shekel lost ground against the dollar, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.06 pct to 107.07
Volume including Makams was 176 million shekels. Turnover in dollar-linked bonds was a moderate 15 million shekels.

"Demand continued for dollar-linked bonds, but at a more moderate pace, with surplus demand of 48 million shekels against 270 million shekels yesterday," said Gidi Halpern of Meitav Investments and Securities.
"The market now believes that the dollar's gains were excessive and that there has to be a retrenchment after the panic. But in practice this has not yet happened," he said.

The Israeli shekel declined for the fourth consecutive session on Wednesday against the dollar, bringing its total loss to about three perecent. The representative rate was fixed at 3.5240 shekels on Wednesday against 3.5060 on Tuesday.
The shekel began tumbling on Friday shortly after the central bank lowered its key lending rate 1.2 percentage points and the cabinet approved exchange rate reforms.

Halpern said prices of CPI-linked short bonds continued higher on Wednesday on fears the dollar's strength would boost inflation. Prices of CPI-linked long bonds were lower on expectations that interest rates would not be cut further and might even rise, he said.
After falling sharply on Tuesday due to concerns that a weaker shekel would fuel inflation, prices of unlinked bonds rose on Wednesday.
"Because of the slowdown in the economy and the unemployment rate no one expects excessive inflationary pressure," said Ilan Doron of Solid Financial markets.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
